results.title: Serving through connection churn (upstream #5211)
results.desc: Exec/DNS/concurrency storm; sandbox must stay alive and keep serving
results.detail: 25 rapid execs ok=25/25; 30x DNS loop clean; 6-wide concurrent all=False; still-Ready=True; post-storm exec ok | diagnostic: owner-token Unauthorized (hsctl session ended 22:12:39Z); retry sandbox timed out reaching Ready in same window
results.prose: Upstream #5211 promises sandboxes survive transient accept errors. I stressed one sandbox with 25 rapid execs (all served), a 30-iteration DNS loop (clean), and then a 6-wide concurrent fan-out — every concurrent stream failed while the sandbox stayed Ready, and a diagnostic retry sandbox timed out reaching Ready in the same window. Sequential serving is solid; the concurrency failure clustered with a gateway-pressure window around 22:10-22:15Z, so I'm recording this as a fail with an inconclusive concurrency verdict rather than a resilience pass. Worth a dedicated retry next cycle.

results.title: Fleet snapshot + drift
results.detail: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) — api-server returned Unauthorized: hsctl session ended 22:12:39Z (invalid_grant after ~9.5h, expires_in shrank 300s→165s first)
results.prose: The fleet snapshot failed with Unauthorized — and the root cause is bigger than this test: the hsctl session itself ended at 22:12:39Z. The refresher log shows the classic Keycloak max-session death spiral: expires_in shrank from 300s to 165s on the 22:08 refresh, then invalid_grant. After ~9.5 hours of continuous rotation, the SSO session max lifetime was hit. The owner needs to re-run hsctl login; fleet stats will fail in every cycle until then.
